source.author: ov
source.text: Iamque fretum Minyae Pagasaea puppe secabant, perpetuaque trahens inopem sub nocte senectam Phineus visus erat, iuvenesque Aquilone creati virgineas volucres miseri senis ore fugarant, multaque perpessi claro sub Iasone tandem contigerant rapidas limosi Phasidos undas.
source.text_original: Iamque fretum Minyae Pagasaea puppe secabant, / perpetuaque trahens inopem sub nocte senectam / Phineus visus erat, iuvenesque Aquilone creati / virgineas volucres miseri senis ore fugarant, / multaque perpessi claro sub Iasone tandem / contigerant rapidas limosi Phasidos undas.
source.text_english: And now the Minyae were cutting the strait in the Pagasaean ship, and Phineus, dragging out an impoverished old age beneath endless night, had appeared; and the young men begotten by Aquilo had driven the maiden-like birds from the wretched old man’s face, and, after suffering much, had at last, under the noble Jason, reached the rushing waters of muddy Phasis.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: taurea vulnifico portat celer aspera plumbo terga Lacon, saltem in vacuos ut bracchia ventos spargat et Oebalium Pagaseia puppis alumnum spectet securo celebrantem litora ludo.
reuse.text_original: taurea vulnifico portat celer aspera plumbo / terga Lacon, saltem in vacuos ut bracchia ventos / spargat et Oebalium Pagaseia puppis alumnum / spectet securo celebrantem litora ludo.
reuse.text_english: The Lacedaemonian, swift, bears on his rough back the bull’s-hide with its wound-making lead, so that at least he may scatter his arms into the empty winds and the Pagasaean ship may watch the Oebalian youth as he sports in safety, making the shore ring with his play.
